# Zeyn

> Zeyn is an open source Rust web framework for data heavy business apps: grids, forms and workflows. AI agents write the application code and people review it. Screens are rendered on the server, so app code has no HTML, CSS or JavaScript. Status: alpha (0.0.3 on crates.io); APIs still change.

## If you are an AI agent asked to build an app with Zeyn

Do not write the project by hand. Install the CLI and let it create the project:

```sh
cargo install zeyn-cli
zeyn new my-app
cd my-app
cargo run
```

The app listens on http://127.0.0.1:3000 (change `server.addr` in `config/app.json`). Then:

1. Read `my-app/AGENTS.md` and `my-app/.claude/skills/zeyn/SKILL.md`. They hold the rules and the patterns for this framework.
2. Add features with `zeyn g feature <name>`; each feature has `models.rs`, `store.rs`, `actions.rs` and `screens.rs`.
3. Run `zeyn check` and `cargo test` after every change. Compiler errors say what to change.
4. `.mcp.json` registers `zeyn mcp`, an MCP server with the tools `zeyn_docs`, `zeyn_describe`, `zeyn_check`, `zeyn_test` and `zeyn_new_feature`.

For a library of features shared by several apps use `zeyn new my-domain --lib`.

Rules that fail the build or the tests if broken: every action and screen declares `permission = "..."` or `public`; every user facing text comes from the locale files (`t!("key")`, English and Turkish); use `DataGrid`, `DataQuery`, `Form` and `Screen` from `zeyn::prelude`, not hand written HTML.
